unit_attributes.choice_text: All of the following three conditions must be satisfied: (1) the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) the employee has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) the employee is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who meets all three criteria: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Provided that the rules governing breaks in service, payroll maintenance, and voluntary employer recognition in 29 CFR 825.110(b)(1) through (b)(4) apply.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the qualifying conditions and rules set forth in 29 CFR 825.110(b) are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where employment periods precede a break in service of more than seven years and either the break was occasioned by USERRA-covered service or a qualifying written agreement exists.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for furthering education or childrearing).
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when absence from work is due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, and subject to the limitation that this section does not provide any greater entitlement than available under USERRA.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer; however, this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
